items.item_text: resume

Coordinate research-based garden education efforts across [County] with a focus on community needs including food gardening, sustainable landscaping, integrated pest management, fire and waterwise landscaping, and other topics.
Represent UCCE and the UC Master Gardener Program in a professional manner.
Engage with the UC ANR Advisor network as subject matter and academic experts contributing to the UC Master Gardener Program.
Develop, maintain and oversee local operating procedures and safety protocols in compliance with UC policies and procedures as needed.
Oversee the full range of program implementation duties for the UC Master Gardener Program within statewide and division-wide guidelines.
Maintain and or oversee an accessible digital presence which may include a website, social media, blogs, newsletters, listservs, and other tools.
Manage and maintain [County] volunteer management software instance.

Perform clerical tasks as necessary to prepare and deliver workshops and training. This may include duplication of materials, maintaining filing systems, organizing and purchasing program related materials and supplies.
Seek and participate in fund development opportunities as needed.
Manage budgets across multiple accounts to ensure program fiscal responsibility
Foster a positive programmatic environment that promotes volunteer learning and leadership and cultivates successful working relationships with volunteers.
Mentor and train UC Master Gardener Program volunteers toward the implementation of impact-focused projects and opportunities.
Coordinate, conduct, and/or oversee delivery of UC Master Gardener Program volunteer training utilizing research-based curricula, materials, forms, and UC ANR content experts.

Progress UC Master Gardener Program volunteer recruitment efforts through utilization of statewide volunteer identification and selection materials, volunteer and county demographic data, and division-wide tools to ensure that core training program benefits are accessible to all.
Develop systems and structures that promote programmatic sustainability through facilitating delegation of tasks/functions to volunteers.
Utilize a developmental approach to volunteer-related conflict. This includes applying mediation techniques, UC ANR policy, and coaching skills to address volunteer-related disputes.
Identify volunteer skills and competencies in order to match volunteers with roles that meet program/community needs.
Develop and maintain volunteer communication systems.
Ensure a strong volunteer appreciation program inclusive of statewide and local recognition.
Develop continuing education and workshops to meet the educational and cultural needs of volunteers (and residents).
Actively promote and market the UC Master Gardener Program to schools, partners, community organizations, and agencies.

Oversee the preparation of lesson materials, and delivery of garden education lessons and demonstrations which respect participants’ cultural and ethnic backgrounds and accessible gardening infrastructure.
Maintain regular, successful communication with partner organizations including agencies, schools, community-based organizations, etc.

Develop liaisons with and between other garden-based learning, environmental education, natural resource, community wellbeing programs and organizations to coordinate outreach efforts. Maintain appropriate records tracking the partnership network.
Develop and implement culturally relevant garden education, project development and partnership strategies.

Ensure collection of volunteer and public participant data (program enrollment, activity tracking, and statewide program evaluation data) using UC ANR approved technologies to measure program delivery and effectiveness.

Work with Advisor, County/Area Director, and UC Master Gardener Program statewide team to analyze evaluation data, generate and contribute to statewide/local reporting, and utilize findings to improve community impact and outcomes.
Ensure quality control and compliance with established standards and procedures for assigned programs.
Assign, monitor and review progress and accuracy of work.
Prepare and provide summaries of evaluation results and progress toward goals.
Maintain team collaboration through meeting/training attendance and consistent written and verbal communication including, but not limited to, weekly schedule, program objectives, and team projects.
Collaborate with other UC ANR programs to coordinate and enhance outreach efforts.
Participate in piloting new curriculum, statewide projects, materials, delivery modes, or evaluation and/or methods.
